Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 33578 of 2023

Applicant :- Mahtab
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjay Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ravi Shankar Yadav
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Sanjay Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ravi Shankar Yadav, learned
counsel for the informant and Sri Tanay Kumar, learned Aga, for the State.
2.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release
him on bail in Case Crime No.134 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366 and 376 Ipc and Section 3/4
Pocso Act, Police Station Bhognipur, District Kanpur Dehat during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 14.4.2022 against the applicant and his family others through an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. dated 14.3.2022 and according to the FIR, on 17.2.2022 applicant enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 18 years.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that the daughter of the informant has also taken Rs.50,000/- and jewellery from her home.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and actually the daughter of the informant is a major girl aged about 18 Mahtab vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56367858/
1 years and she according to her own wish had gone along with applicant and this fact is evident from her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further submits that although as per FIR applicant enticed away the daughter of the informant on 17.2.2022 but in spite of that application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved on 14.3.2022,
i.e., for almost a month and this fact clearly suggests that after about a month totally on the basis of false allegation applicant and his family members have been made accused in the present matter.
6. He further submits that during investigation due to refusal of the prosecutrix her radiological age could not be ascertained but according to her High School Certificate she was around 17 years old at the time of incident.
7.

He further submits that it is a case of love affair and applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 19.3.2023, i.e., for the last almost six months.

8. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayerfor bail and submitted that as according to the school record victim was hardly 17 years old at the time of incident, therefore, her consent is immaterial.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Although, from the High School Certificate of the prosecutrix it appears that she was around 17 years old at the time of incident but admittedly she did not make any allegation of rape against the applicant in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.and due to her refusal, her ossification test could not be conducted.
11. Further FIR of the present case was lodged on an application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. and even application moved under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved after almost a month.
12. The law is settled that bail application should not be dismissed either for punitive or preventive purposes.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant-Mahtab be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
